title: Adaptive Runway & Initiative Stitching for Hosted API + Model Catalog (Quarterly Planning)
creator: Nora Patel
description:
Objective: define a single, adaptive quarterly runway that stitches together hosted API feature priorities with model catalog phasing across customer cohorts. This ticket captures the plan, decision gates, and operational handoffs needed to convert strategy into deterministic execution for Q3.

Background: past quarters have separated hosted API prioritization from model lineup decisions; that has led to mismatched rollouts (new model variants landing without SDK or routing support) and avoidable customer migration friction. This work creates a unified roadmap artifact and a cadence for reconciling capacity, canary windows, and evaluation gates.

Scope:
- Product-level prioritization across the hosted API surface (streaming, structured output, function/tool calling) tied to model variants that satisfy cost/latency trade-offs.
- Cohort phasing: define three customer cohort paths (PLG early adopters, mid-market pilot, enterprise safe rollout) and their timing/windows.
- Initiative stitching: coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams for capacity hedges and with Runtime/Eng for kernel/quantization compatibility windows.
- Deliverables: a public roadmap artifact for internal stakeholders, a gating checklist per model variant, a canary schedule, and an acceptance criteria matrix.

Key decisions to make in this ticket:
- Which model variants are eligible for host-level default routing vs opt-in experimental lanes.
- Canary sizing targets (traffic %, duration) per cohort and per endpoint.
- Rollout fallback policy when latency or quality regressions are detected.

Stakeholders: PM (owner), Runtime Eng, Dedicated Capacity, Console/Observability, Applied ML (model onboarding), Solutions/SE.

Expected outcome: a single master roadmap artifact that product, eng, and go-to-market can reference for execution and escalations; reduces cross-team unblock cycles by 40% (target).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Master roadmap artifact published in Confluence with explicit cohort timelines and canary windows.
2) Gating checklist for each model variant with responsible owners and measurable thresholds (p95 latency, top-line quality regression threshold, cost delta).
3) Cross-team signoffs from Runtime, Dedicated, and Console teams recorded in comments.
4) Two-week trial canary schedule drafted and resourced for at least one model swap scenario.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (Discovery, weeks 1-2): validate cohort segmentation and capacity assumptions; run synthetic load to confirm throughput targets.
Phase B (Canary pilot, weeks 3-4): pick a low-risk model variant + single PLG cohort; 48hr canary at 2% traffic, expand to 10% on green metrics.
Phase C (Gradual expansion, weeks 5-9): open mid-market cohort with 7-day canaries and enterprise pilots behind dedicated routing & SLA checks.
Phase D (GA readiness, week 10): final signoffs, monitoring dashboards live, rollback playbooks verified.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Model variant introduces quality regression for enterprise prompts. Mitigation: require pre-rollout evals against enterprise prompt sets and block enterprise cohort until evaluation threshold reached.
Risk: Dedicated capacity shortage during staggered rollouts. Mitigation: prebook buffer capacity and plan burst-to-hosted fallback routes.
Risk: Observability gaps (token-level cost/latency). Mitigation: Console team to enable temporary retention on relevant traces and expose route-specific dashboards for the canary period.
metrics:
Primary metrics: p95 latency (ms) per endpoint, cost per 1M tokens, model-prompt quality score delta (eval suite), availability/SLO. Secondary metrics: canary error rate, rollback frequency, time-to-detect regressions.
Targets: p95 latency change <= +15% vs baseline; quality regression <= 1.5% on critical prompt sets; cost delta <= +10% before negotiated product approval.
